lessons.title: Making new friends
lessons.goal: I can talk about making new friends.

newItems.example: Their friendship is very strong.
He is easy-going and fun.

newItems.definition: A person you know, but not well.
newItems.example: He is an old acquaintance of mine.
We hit it off on the first day.
I want to get to know my new friend.

lessons.mainWordForms: Friendship is a noun. Friendship means a close feeling between friends. Their friendship is very strong.
lessons.expression: We hit it off on the first day.
lessons.use: Use this when you talk about liking a new friend at once.
lessons.expressionTask: Tom and Lily talk about new friends. What do they say?
lessons.grammar: present simple for facts about friends: A good friend is kind
context: Tom and Lily talk about new friends.
Tom says, 'We hit it off on the first day. Our friendship is very strong.'
dialogue: Lily, do you like your new friend?
Yes. We hit it off on the first day. He is easy-going and fun.
What is friendship?
It is a close feeling between friends. Our friendship is very strong.
Do you know him well?
Not yet. I want to get to know someone new. He is an old acquaintance of my brother.
lessons.listening: Tom and Lily talk about new friends. Tom says, 'We hit it off on the first day. Our friendship is very strong.' Lily says, 'What is friendship?' Tom says, 'It is a close feeling between friends.' Lily says, 'Do you know him well?' Tom says, 'Not yet. I want to get to know someone new.'
lessons.question: What is friendship?
lessons.reading: On Monday, Tom and Lily talk about new friends. Tom says, 'We hit it off on the first day. Our friendship is very strong. He is easy-going and fun, and he likes school.' Lily says, 'What is friendship?' Tom says, 'It is a close feeling between friends. I want to get to know someone new. He is an old acquaintance of my brother, and now he is my friend too.' Lily says, 'That is good. New friends make school happy.' Tom says, 'Yes. I meet new people at school, and I like it.' Lily says, 'Do you like your new friend?' Tom says, 'Yes. He is easy-going, and we talk every day at school.'
lessons.readingQ: When did Tom and Lily hit it off?
lessons.speaking: Tell a friend about a new friend. What do you say?
lessons.speakingSample: I talk about my new friend with my friend Tom. We hit it off on the first day. Our friendship is very strong. He is easy-going and fun. I want to get to know someone new. He is an old acquaintance of my brother. I meet new people at school, and I like it.
lessons.writing: Write a short email to a friend about a new friend. Say how you met.
lessons.writingSample: Dear Anna, I want to tell you about my new friend. We hit it off on the first day. Our friendship is very strong. He is easy-going and fun. I want to get to know someone new. He is an old acquaintance of my brother. I meet new people at school. He likes school, and we talk every day at school. I am happy to have a new friend. See you soon. Best, Lily
lessons.sound: Friendship has its strongest beat on FRIEND. In friendship, say FRIEND clearly at the start. In acquaintance, say QUAINT clearly in the middle.

Yes. I am an extrovert. I like to meet people and play.

He is an introvert. He likes time alone, but we hang out with our friends on Sunday.

mainWord.definition: A friend you write letters to.

lessons.mainWordForms: Pen pal is a noun. Pen pal means a friend you write letters to. My pen pal lives in Canada.

context: Tom and Lily talk about keeping in touch.
Tom says, 'Let us catch up with our old friends. We are meeting on Sunday.'
dialogue: Lily, do you write to your pen pal?
Yes. My pen pal lives in Canada. I write a letter every week.
How do you keep in touch?
I call and write. I drop someone a line when I am free.
What about Tom?
He is sympathetic and listens well. I want to get back in touch with Tom.

newItems.example: She is a caring friend.

newItems.definition: To do something kind for someone.

lessons.mainWordForms: Caring is an adjective. Caring means kind and thinking about others. She is a caring friend.
lessons.expression: Can you lend a hand with this?
lessons.use: Use this when you ask someone to help you.

Tom says, 'Can you lend a hand with this? I will help you.'
dialogue: Tom, do you need help?
Yes, please. Can you lend a hand with this?
Of course. I will help you. I am a caring friend.
Thank you. You are kind-hearted.
A good friend will do someone a favor.
I want to cheer someone up today.

mainWord.definition: To understand something in the wrong way.

lessons.mainWordForms: Misunderstand is a verb. Misunderstand means to understand something in the wrong way. Do not misunderstand my words.
lessons.use: Use this when you talk about a problem with a friend.
lessons.expressionTask: Tom and Lily talk about saying sorry. What do they say?
lessons.grammar: should and shouldn't for advice: You should say sorry
context: Tom and Lily talk about saying sorry.
Tom says, 'Let us talk things over. You should say sorry.'
dialogue: Lily, are you angry?
Yes. I am sad. You misunderstand my words.
I am sorry. Let us talk things over.
Good. Do not listen to gossip. You can lean on someone when you are sad.
Thank you. I should not be jealous of my friend.
You should say sorry when you are wrong.
lessons.listening: Tom and Lily talk about saying sorry. Tom says, 'Lily, are you angry?' Lily says, 'Yes. I am sad. You misunderstand my words.' Tom says, 'I am sorry. Let us talk things over.' Lily says, 'Good. Do not listen to gossip. You can lean on someone when you are sad.'

I should not be jealous of my friend. I listen and understand.' Tom says, 'I understand. I will listen to you.' Lily says, 'Thank you. We can talk every day. I am happy to have a good friend.' Tom says, 'Friends help each other. I will help you at home and at school.'
